name: Gera
overview: Gera was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, noted in Scripture primarily as the son of Ehud. He is uniquely identified in 1 Chronicles 8:6 as one who "carried them into exile," indicating a role connected to the exile of his people. There are no additional notes about his character or actions beyond this attribute.
namesAndTitles: The name Gera, appearing four times in Scripture, is a proper name that may mean "sojourner," though this meaning is not definitively given by God. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:7 without further titles or distinctions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Gera as the son of Ehud. Inferred relationships suggest that Ehud was the son of Uzzah, who was the son of Ahihud, and Ahihud was the son of Shaharaim, establishing Gera's lineage within the Benjaminite clan as detailed in 1 Chronicles 8:7-8.
scriptureSignificance: Gera's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his connection to the exile, as he is described as having "carried them into exile," a phrase that implies involvement in a critical moment of Israel's history. His mention within the genealogical records of Benjamin underscores the continuity of God's covenant people through trials such as exile. While brief, his record contributes to the broader biblical theme of God's faithfulness to His people amid judgment and displacement.
